summary.text: Joe Courtney is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Connecticut's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2006, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.
A lawyer and former public defender, he served in the Connecticut House of Representatives from 1987 to 1994 before entering Congress.
He serves on the House Armed Services and Education and Workforce committees and is ranking member of the Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and Projection Forces.

paragraphs.text: Courtney was born in Hartford County, Connecticut, and graduated from Northwest Catholic High School. He earned a bachelor's degree from Tufts University in 1975 and a law degree from the University of Connecticut School of Law in 1978.
He worked as a public defender before entering the legislature.
Courtney represented Vernon in the Connecticut House of Representatives from 1987 to 1994, serving as House chairman of both the Public Health and Human Services committees.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 2006 and has represented Connecticut's 2nd District since 2007, currently serving his tenth term.

He serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee, and chaired the Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and Projection Forces from 2018 to 2022 before becoming its ranking member. His official biography says he is the first known Connecticut member to lead a House naval oversight panel since 1873.

His official biography says he has worked for increased submarine production, which it credits with sustaining Electric Boat's workforce in southeastern Connecticut, and that he received the Navy's Distinguished Public Service Award from Navy Secretary Ray Mabus.

Courtney is the founding co-chairman of the Congressional Dairy Farmers Caucus, and the biography says he introduced the law designating the Eightmile River as part of the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System.
According to the same biography, he lives in Vernon with his wife, Audrey, and their two children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 62.5% of the vote to George Austin's 37.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
